title: ok26jr
Fadak and Lady Fatima's Estrangement
hook: Fadak, which the Prophet had given to his daughter, was taken from her hand. She stated her right through a verse and died estranged.
scenes.0.text: To the north of Medina, near Khyber, there was a fruitful palm tree called Fedak. The people here made a pact not to fight the Muslims. Land taken without a battle would be left directly to the Prophet. The Prophet gave this garden to his daughter **Fatima** and left it to her. A gift is a free gift of something. Fadak's palm trees brought fertility to Fatima's house every year. This income covered most of the livelihood of the Ahl al-Bayt. When the Prophet passed away, **Ali** presided over his funeral and the family was in deep mourning. At the same time, a new account was opened for Fadak, while the bidding was taking place in Sakife.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.1.text: Shortly after the Prophet's death, the C**aliph** Abu Bakr seized Fedak. **Fatima** demanded the return of the land her father had given her. First, he said Fadak was donated to him. When this was refused, she demanded her inheritance as her father's daughter. Both requests were denied. According to the Shiite reading, this handshake wasn't just a matter of possessions. Fadak's income kept the Ehl-i-Beyt strong. If this income was taken from them, Ali would not have the strength to defend his right to the caliphate. For Fatima, it was about her father's word and her own right.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.2.text: Then **Fatimah** went to the Prophet's mosque. The mosque was packed, and the congregation was eager to hear what he had to say. It was there that Fatima delivered what was later called the Fedak Sermon. It was the voice of a daughter who had just lost her father, but it was the voice of someone who knew what was right. And his word was fulfilled: 'We will not inherit the Prophets. It's the charity we left behind". Fatima answered with the Quran. In verse 16 of the Surah of Naml, he reminded that Solomon was David's heir, and in verse 6 of the Surah of Mary, he asked that Zechariah's son John be his heir. If the sons of the prophets can inherit, why can't the Prophet's daughter?
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.3.text: After the sermon, **Fatima** brought two witnesses to prove that the Fedak was given to her. One was his wife, **Ali**. The other was Umm Eymen. Umm Eymen was an elderly woman in the Prophet's house who took care of him in his childhood. Both witnesses said that the Prophet gave the Fedak to Fatima. But their testimony was not accepted. Ali's word was not enough. Umm Eymen's promise was not enough. But the garden had been in the hands of Fatima for years. It was an open injustice in Medina to demand a document from a person in possession of property.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.3.art.actors.2.label: 19dj5z1
Umm Ayman
scenes.4.text: The Prophet said of his daughter: "My ransom is part of me. Whoever angers him angers me". This hadith is also accepted as authentic in Sunni sources. When the deposition was denied and the witnesses were turned away, **Fatima** was angry with the caliph Abu Bakr. She never spoke to him again after that day. According to Buhari's story, this resentment lasted until his death. Fatima's resentment was not a momentary rage. His father's donation, the inheritance he defended with the Qur'an and the testimony of the witnesses he brought were all rejected. The girl, to whom the Prophet said, "Whoever angers him angers me", spent all her days after her father's death with this resentment.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.5.text: Six months after the Prophet's death, **Fatima** passed away. His resentment continued after his death. **Ali** washed her at night, made her pray, and buried her in the dark. The Caliph did not inform Abu Bakr. This detail goes for Buhari. Fatima did not want to attend the funeral of those who hurt her, and Ali complied. When morning came, the people of Medina learned that the Prophet's daughter had been buried, but no one knew where her grave was. Fatima's last days, what happened in front of her door and her secret tomb are told in the story titled Eyyam-i Fatimiye.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.text: Fadak's story didn't end with Fatima's death. Years later, the Emevi Caliph Umar b. Abdulaziz returned Fadak to the descendants of Fatima. The caliph who came after him took back the garden. The Abbasid caliph **Me'mun** also returned the Fedak once again to Fatima's grandchildren. The garden has changed hands over the centuries to suit the taste of the caliphs. But each return was actually an admission that Fatima was right. Shiites today remember Fadak as a halal possession left to the Prophet's daughter and taken from her by force. The name of a palm tree has become a symbol of injustice to the Ahl-i Beyt.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: xt2qi8
Umar b. Abd al-Aziz
sunni.0.says: Lady Fatima asks Caliph Abu Bakr for her inheritance; she is refused; Lady Fatima becomes angry and remains estranged until she dies; Imam Ali buries her at night, does not inform Caliph Abu Bakr; Imam Ali later pledges allegiance.
sunni.1.says: Parallel narrations of the same event: the inheritance request and the answer "prophets do not leave inheritance."
sunni.2.says: Caliph Abu Bakr's narration about the Prophet's inheritance and Lady Fatima's request.
sunni.3.says: "Lady Fatima is a part of me; whoever angers her has angered me."
sunni.4.says: The return of Fadak to Lady Fatima's descendants by Umar b. Abd al-Aziz and al-Ma'mun.
shia.0.says: The gift of Fadak to Lady Fatima as a hiba, and the witnesses.
shia.0.grade: This is the usurping interpretation of the Shiite school that the handcuff is read out of fear of the caliphate.
shia.1.says: The Fadak sermon that Lady Fatima delivered in the mosque. Neml 16 and Meryem 6, as the answer to the inheritance of the children of prophets, are in the Shia reading of this sermon.
shia.2.says: The tensions in the process of the pledge of allegiance.
disputes.0.title: za2e8g
To whom did Fadak belong?
disputes.0.sunni: Fadak was land taken without war and was at the Prophet's disposal. In the Sunni reading, after the Prophet it is the state's charity.
disputes.0.shia: Fadak was land taken without a fight. In Shia reading, the Prophet gave it to Fatimah and left it as an inheritance. The seizure is read as making the Ahl-i-Bait economically weak and cutting off Ali's ability to defend his right to the caliphate.
disputes.1.title: qzb3z3
"Prophets do not leave inheritance"
disputes.1.sunni: The saying "Prophets do not leave inheritance" appears in Bukhari as a narration of Caliph Abu Bakr. In the Sunni reading, the hadith is sahih. The inheritance verses in the Qur'an are regarded as an inheritance of knowledge and prophethood.
disputes.1.shia: Lady Fatima sets Neml 16 and Meryem 6 against this saying: Solomon inherited from David, Yahya from Zechariah. Imam Ali and Umm Ayman were brought as witnesses, and their words were not accepted.
disputes.2.title: 1nvqs0p
Lady Fatima's estrangement
disputes.2.sunni: Bukhari 4240 reports that Lady Fatima remained estranged until her death and was buried at night.
disputes.2.shia: This estrangement combines with the taking of the gifted Fadak and the rejection of the sermon and the testimony. The saying "Whoever angers her has angered me" makes this pain the Prophet's pain.
questions.0: She went to the mosque for Fatima Fadak and recalled the Neml 16 and Maryam 6. Why do you think Fatima responded with these two verses when she said, "We don't inherit the prophets"?
questions.1: Fadak had been in Fatima's possession for years and Ali and Ummu Eymen testified in her favor, but their testimony was not accepted. Why do you think the person holding the property was asked for a document anyway?
questions.2: When the deposition was denied and the witnesses were turned away, Fatima was angry with Caliph Abu Bekir. Why do you think that resentment lasted until his death?
summary: The Prophet gave Fedak to Fatima and left it to her as an inheritance. It was confiscated by Caliph Abu Bakr. Fatima answered with Neml 16 and Mary 6 in the mosque. The testimony of Ali and Umm Eymen was not accepted. He died of grief. Buhari writes 4240 bitterness and nightly funeral. And the witnesses are in the record. It is in the Book of Nisa.
notes.0: Fadak was a village near Khaybar that came to terms without fighting and was at the Prophet's disposal.
notes.1: Lady Fatima asked Caliph Abu Bakr for Fadak and her share of the inheritance.
notes.2: Caliph Abu Bakr refused with the hadith «We prophets do not leave inheritance.»
notes.3: Lady Fatima became estranged over this and did not speak until her death (Bukhari 4240).
notes.4: Fadak was later returned by Umar b. Abd al-Aziz.
sunni.5.says: When Israa 26 ("Give your due to your relatives") descended, the Prophet called Fatimah and gave her the Fedak. The Sunni mainstream considers this legend weak.
sunni.6.says: Fatima's Fedak sermon at the mosque. Ibn Tayfûr (died c. 280) is a Sunni literary figure and the earliest known written source of the sermon. Sunni hadith is not in the mainstream.
